strings.d1.s0.name: Jama Masjid
strings.d1.s0.tips: India's largest mosque. Buy a minaret ticket for the view. Cover shoulders and knees, and leave your shoes outside.
strings.d1.s1.name: Chandni Chowk
strings.d1.s1.tips: Old Delhi's main market. Take a rickshaw through the narrow lanes and visit the Khari Baoli spice market.
strings.d1.s2.name: Paranthe Wali Gali
strings.d1.s2.tips: A lane of stuffed parathas fried in ghee, open since the 1870s. Expect 3-4 varieties.
strings.d1.s3.name: Red Fort
strings.d1.s3.tips: Shah Jahan's red fortress. UNESCO site, 600 INR for foreigners, closed on Mondays.
strings.d1.s4.name: Karim's Jama Masjid
strings.d1.s4.tips: Mughal cooking since 1913. Order the mutton burra and nihari, on the lane facing the mosque.
strings.d1.b0.name: Al Jawahar Restaurant
strings.d1.b0.tips: Karim's rival across the road. Kebabs and korma.
strings.d1.b1.name: Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib
strings.d1.b1.tips: A Sikh temple on Chandni Chowk. Free langar (community meal); enter with your head covered.
strings.d2.s0.name: Humayun's Tomb
strings.d2.s0.tips: The Mughal tomb that preceded the Taj Mahal. Go for the morning light and the gardens.
strings.d2.s1.name: Nizamuddin Dargah
strings.d2.s1.tips: A Sufi shrine. Qawwali music on Thursday evenings, set among narrow lanes.
strings.d2.s2.name: Lodhi Garden
strings.d2.s2.tips: A park among 15th-century tombs. The calmest spot in Delhi.
strings.d2.s3.name: Khan Market
strings.d2.s3.tips: A stylish market. Try the kathi roll at Khan Chacha and browse the bookshops.
strings.d2.s4.name: India Gate
strings.d2.s4.tips: War memorial on Rajpath. In the evening it fills with families and ice cream.
strings.d2.b0.name: Sodabottleopenerwala Khan Market
strings.d2.b0.tips: A Parsi cafe. Try the berry pulao.
strings.d2.b1.name: National Museum Delhi
strings.d2.b1.tips: Harappan finds and Mughal miniatures. An indoor option in the heat.
strings.d3.s0.name: Qutub Minar
strings.d3.s0.tips: A 73 m minaret from the 12th century, with a rust-free iron pillar. Cooler in the morning.
strings.d3.s1.name: Mehrauli Archaeological Park
strings.d3.s1.tips: A free ruins park next to Qutub Minar. Look for Jamali Kamali.
strings.d3.s2.name: Hauz Khas Village
strings.d3.s2.tips: Lakeside madrasa ruins, boutiques and cafes.
strings.d3.s3.name: Hauz Khas Social
strings.d3.s3.tips: A cafe-bar with lake views. Good for lunch.
strings.d3.s4.name: Lotus Temple
strings.d3.s4.tips: The Baha'i lotus-shaped temple. Quiet inside; closed on Mondays.
strings.d3.b0.name: Naivedyam Hauz Khas
strings.d3.b1.name: Dilli Haat INA
strings.d3.b1.tips: A market of handicrafts and regional cuisines. An alternative to the temple.
strings.d4.s0.name: Taj Mahal
strings.d4.s0.tips: Take the Gatimaan Express at 08:10 (1.5 hours) or leave by car at 05:00. Sunrise ticket 1,100 + 200 for the mausoleum; closed Fridays; shoe covers are provided.
strings.d4.s1.name: Agra Fort
strings.d4.s1.tips: The fort where Shah Jahan was imprisoned. See the Taj across the river.
strings.d4.s2.name: Pinch of Spice Agra
strings.d4.s2.tips: North Indian cuisine in Agra. Air-conditioned.
strings.d4.s3.name: Itmad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj)
strings.d4.s3.tips: A small tomb that pioneered marble inlay. No crowds.
strings.d4.s4.name: Mehtab Bagh
strings.d4.s4.tips: A garden on the opposite bank of the river. Sunset view of the Taj; return train at 18:00.
strings.d4.b0.name: Joney's Place Agra
strings.d4.b0.tips: A backpacker classic. Try the lassi.
strings.d4.b1.name: Fatehpur Sikri
strings.d4.b1.tips: An abandoned Mughal capital (40 km). An alternative to Baby Taj.
strings.d5.s0.name: Amber Fort
strings.d5.s0.tips: 4-5 hours from Delhi by train or car (ideal with an overnight stay). Mirror palace on the hilltop; take a jeep instead of an elephant.
strings.d5.s1.name: Hawa Mahal
strings.d5.s1.tips: The facade of the Palace of Winds. Take photos from the cafe opposite.
strings.d5.s2.name: City Palace Jaipur
strings.d5.s2.tips: The Maharaja's palace and museum. The heart of the Pink City.
strings.d5.s3.name: Laxmi Misthan Bhandar
strings.d5.s3.tips: A sweet shop and restaurant since 1727. Order dal baati and ghewar.
strings.d5.s4.name: Johari Bazaar
strings.d5.s4.tips: A market for jewellery and block-printed fabric. Bargain.
strings.d5.b0.name: Jantar Mantar Jaipur
strings.d5.b0.tips: Giant stone astronomical instruments. An alternative to the palace.
strings.d5.b1.name: Rawat Misthan Bhandar
strings.d5.b1.tips: Pyaz kachori (fried onion-stuffed pastry), Jaipur's street food favourite.
strings.d6.s0.name: Akshardham Temple
strings.d6.s0.tips: A vast modern Hindu temple complex. Phones and cameras are not allowed (leave them in the cloakroom); exhibitions around 250 INR.
strings.d6.s1.name: Connaught Place
strings.d6.s1.tips: A circular market with white colonnades. The centre of Delhi.
strings.d6.s2.name: Saravana Bhavan Connaught Place
strings.d6.s2.tips: South Indian thali and dosa. Air-conditioned.
strings.d6.s3.name: Janpath Market
strings.d6.s4.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
strings.d6.s4.tips: A Sikh temple with a golden dome and sacred pool. Visit the langar kitchen.
strings.d6.b0.name: Kake Da Hotel Connaught
strings.d6.b1.name: Agrasen ki Baoli
strings.d6.b1.tips: A stepwell. Good photos, near Janpath.
strings.d7.theme: Morning market and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Sunder Nursery
strings.d7.s0.tips: A restored Mughal garden next to Humayun's Tomb. Morning walk; organic market on Sundays.
strings.d7.s1.name: Cafe Lota Pragati Maidan
strings.d7.s1.tips: Modern Indian breakfast and lunch in the garden of the crafts museum. A farewell meal.
strings.d7.s2.name: National Crafts Museum
strings.d7.s2.tips: A crafts museum with master artisans' stalls. Good for souvenirs.
strings.d7.s3.name: Delhi Metro Airport Express
strings.d7.s3.tips: 20 minutes from New Delhi station to the airport. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Andhra Bhavan Canteen
strings.d7.b0.tips: Cheap unlimited thali. A Delhi legend.
strings.d7.b1.name: Purana Qila
strings.d7.b1.tips: The Old Fort and its lake. An alternative to the museum.
strings.note0: The Delhi Metro is clean, cheap and air-conditioned (with a women's carriage). Uber and Ola are safe; bargain with auto-rickshaw drivers. Take the Gatimaan Express to Agra and the Shatabdi to Jaipur.
strings.note1: October to March is the best season (15-25°C). Mornings from November to January bring fog and air pollution. Wear a mask and allow for train delays.
strings.note2: Monument entry costs foreigners 500-600 INR (35 for Indians). An online ASI ticket skips the queue. The Taj is closed on Fridays, the Red Fort on Mondays.
strings.note3: Choose street food that is cooked and hot, and skip ice and raw salads. Drink bottled water. Take probiotics against Delhi belly.
strings.note4: Remove your shoes in temples and mosques, and cover shoulders and knees. Enter Sikh gurdwaras with your head covered; the food is free.
strings.note5: Tip 10%. Bargaining works everywhere: start at a third of the first price.
